text:
maria: FYI customer ACME reported sudden p99 spikes (~3s) starting ~09:15 UTC, only for requests routed to eu-west. They say it started after the morning deploy.
infra-bot: alert: routing-anomaly detected for tenant=acme, spike=api.p99>2.5s, region=eu-west, affected_hosts=redwood-eu-prod-*/egress
sam: Can you attach a trace/packet output? If it's cross-region egress we'll see a hop into AP/SA.
maria: Attaching a quick traceroute the customer ran:
```
traceroute to api.redwood.example (52.17.88.10), 30 hops max, 60 byte packets
 1  10.0.0.1  0.123 ms  0.112 ms  0.111 ms
 2  172.16.5.1  0.45 ms  0.36 ms  0.37 ms
 3  * * *
 4  34.210.66.5 (34.210.66.5)  25.632 ms  25.629 ms  25.632 ms  AS16509
 5  13.52.123.1 (13.52.123.1)  190.772 ms  190.761 ms  190.756 ms  AS16509  <- unexpected AS/region (ap-south)
 6  52.17.88.10 (52.17.88.10)  191.001 ms  190.992 ms  190.989 ms
```
Note the big jump at hop 5 into AP region.
josh: That hop (13.52.123.1) is a cloud egress via our partner peer in AP-SOUTH. Could be BGP flap or a route leak pushing prefixes via that peer.
alice: Quick repro steps I ran from our eu-prod node (eu-app-07):
```
# run a few requests to the model endpoint and measure p99
for i in {1..50}; do curl -s -D - -o /dev/null -H "X-Region: eu-west" "https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate?model=rw-large"; done
```
Observed ~200ms normally, then a subset ~1.8-2.0s when kernel IP path shifted. Logs show our egress IP mapped to an AP geolocation: `geoip: ap-south-1` and our auth service occasionally returned 403 for some tokens during the high-latency period.
sam: 403s + geoip mismatch suggests upstream NAT or SNATing via a different POP. Can you paste the HTTP response headers from one of the slow responses?
maria: Header excerpt from slow request: `X-Forwarded-For: 18.201.34.12`, `X-Client-Region: eu-west`, `X-Observed-Egress: 13.52.123.1`, `Auth-Result: 403`, `X-Trace-Id: trace-0a3b`
kevin: That X-Observed-Egress IP is in our partner ASN for ap-south. I'm guessing our peering that usually takes eu prefixes briefly announced a more specific route to that peer, causing EU egress to leak. Could be a BGP community change during last night's config push.
josh: Can we confirm by checking BGP collectors? I'll query the routeviews looking glass for the prefix 52.17.88.0/24.
sam: I ran a quick bgp lookup: majority of peers still show announcement via eu transit, but two peers (one major ISP, one partner) briefly chose the path via AS45678 (partner ap-south) at 09:14:21 UTC. That timestamp aligns to the customer's spikes.
alice: Repro (from eu-app-07) with trace enabled shows where routing changed mid-connection: `TRACE: egress-ip=13.52.123.1 (ap-south) at 09:14:22`. Captured bytes show no packet loss, just longer latency due to the detour.
kevin: Proposed mitigation: 1) add a short-term BGP community to prefer eu peers for our critical prefixes (force-local), 2) pin affected Dedicated tenants to regional egress via sticky routing policy, 3) open ticket with partner ASN to debug the unexpected more-specific announcement.
maria: Can we do (1) now? We need a quick mitigation for ACME and couple other customers.
sam: I've pushed a BGP community to origin for the /24s to prefer eu egress (rolling change, should converge within minutes). Will monitor. @infra-bot can you watch p99 for acme?
infra-bot: action: bgp-community applied to prefixes [52.17.88.0/24], monitor=tenant=acme, window=15m.
( ~8 minutes pass )
infra-bot: update: tenant=acme p99 decreased from 2.1s -> 210ms over 6 minutes after community change. No further 403s detected.
maria: Customer confirmed latency normalized, no auth errors. Thanks. :tada:
sam: Follow-ups: file a postmortem with timeline + partner contact, add an automatic detection rule for sudden geoip change for egress IPs (if egress geo != request region && p99>500ms -> alert), and consider a permanent sticky routing flag for Dedicated customers.
josh: I'll grab BGP dumps and dump them into the incident folder.
alice: I'll add a repro notebook for support to run quick traceroutes + curl checks.
kevin: I'll open the partner ticket and cc network ops.
maria: Closing the thread—reassigning to incidents for tracking. :white_check_mark:
